title: Incremental role handoff and audit-stream migration: phased switchover with log-forwarding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Move accounts from RBAC v1 role-store to RBAC v2 with minimal disruption, preserve a complete audit trail, and enable SSO/SAML role mapping continuity. This ticket covers an incremental handoff approach: a write-through bridge for role changes, real-time audit log streaming to the centralized audit pipeline, and a staged canary promotion that minimizes blast radius for customer-facing authorization changes. The emphasis is on observability, test harnesses for role equivalence, and clear rollback windows for each phase.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Role changes performed in v1 are guaranteed to appear in v2 within 5 minutes during write-through mode
2) Audit events for role/read/write operations are emitted to the central audit topic in both schemas (v1-compatible envelope + v2 metadata)
3) Canary group (10% of orgs) sees no authorization errors after 48 hours and key SLOs (auth latency <20ms, error rate <0.1%) are met
4) Automated reconciliation run shows <0.01% role-model divergence after backfill window
5) Customer-facing admin UI shows a migration status indicator and safe rollback button
rollout_steps: A. Deploy write-through bridge service (read from v1, write to v2) behind feature flag
B. Start audit-stream adapter to publish v2 audit events alongside v1 events to central topic
C. Run initial backfill for historical role objects into v2 using throttled workers
D. Enable canary for synthetic orgs and 10% live orgs with strict observability hooks
E. Monitor metrics for 48 hours, run reconciliation checks, and solicit QA/PM signoff
F. Promote canary to 50% then 100% if all gates pass; flip deprecation flag on v1 reads only after full promotion
rollback_steps: 1) Flip feature flag to revert to v1-only writes (bridge stops writing to v2)
2) Disable audit-stream adapter to prevent divergent auditing while restoring previous pipeline
3) Run targeted reconciliation for any orgs that experienced drift and reapply v1 canonical state
4) Open incident runbook and notify affected customers with proposed mitigation timeline
risks: A. Time lag between writes could create temporary authorization mismatches for high-frequency role updates
B. Schema divergence in audit events could break downstream log consumers if not version tolerant
C. Large-scale backfill can overload DB or increase request quotas, affecting production latency
D. SSO/SAML role mapping edge cases may surface only for specific enterprise mappings
E. Customer admins may perform concurrent manual edits during cutover causing race conditions
mitigations: - Implement per-org write queuing and bounded retries to limit burst load
- Emit both v1-compatible and v2-augmented audit envelopes; add consumer feature flags
- Throttle backfill workers by CPU/DB P95 metrics and maintain a kill-switch
- Pre-run a SAML role-mapping verifier against top 50 enterprise configs
- Lock admin UI edits for orgs in active migration window and display clear migration notices
monitoring_gates: - Authz mismatch rate (v1 vs v2) < 0.05% over 2 hours
- Audit event delivery latency median < 2s and 99th < 30s
- Backfill worker DB write error rate < 0.01%
- SSO mapping verification failures = 0 for canary orgs
tests: - Replay test harness comparing policy decisions between v1 and v2 for recorded sessions
- Chaos test: induce read-repair delays to verify graceful degradation
- End-to-end QA for admin console showing migration state and rollback path
- Integration tests for audit consumer backwards compatibility
